title: Opening or deleting a note by keyboard destroys the focused button, so focus falls to the page body
evidence: Driven: focused '#list .open', pressed Enter; document.activeElement was BODY. Same after Enter on '#list .del'. renderList rebuilds every button on each selectNote/deleteNote and each autosave (app.js:49, 100).
failing_case: A keyboard user tabs to a note and presses Enter. Focus is lost to <body>; the next Tab restarts at the top of the page, so reaching the editor means tabbing back through the search box, New note and every note row. A screen reader announces nothing for the opened note. After Delete the same happens. WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order.
remediation: Record the focused button's data-id and class before replaceChildren and refocus the matching new button afterwards. After a delete, focus the next row or the New note button. Better, reconcile list items instead of rebuilding them.

title: Every save overwrites the whole store from one tab's stale in-memory list, so a second tab's notes are erased
evidence: Driven with Playwright in one browser context: tab B created 'from B' and storage held ['first','from B']; tab A (loaded earlier) then edited a note and, 500 ms later, storage held only ['first']. There is no 'storage' event listener, and saveNotes writes the full array each time (app.js:33).
failing_case: Open the app in two tabs. Create a note in tab B. Switch to tab A and edit any note. After the 500 ms debounce, tab A writes its own list over the stored one. The note made in tab B is gone from storage with no message, and tab A shows 'Saved'.
remediation: Re-read storage and merge by note id (or compare a revision counter) before each write, and listen for the 'storage' event to refresh the in-memory list. Show a conflict message if a merge is not possible.

title: 'Search notes' matches titles only, so a word in a note's text finds nothing
evidence: Driven: a note with body 'milk' and title 'Untitled'; searching 'milk' showed 0 rows and 'No notes match "milk".' The control is labelled 'Search notes' (index.html:14).
failing_case: User writes 'milk, eggs' in a note titled 'Shopping', searches 'milk', and is told no notes match. They may conclude the note was lost.
remediation: Match against title and body, or relabel the field 'Search titles' and make the empty message say 'No titles match'.

quote: try { localStorage.setItem(BACKUP_KEY, raw); } catch (e) { /* storage is already failing; the load message says so */ }
title: Backup failure is swallowed while the load message says the data 'was kept', and the next save then destroys the original
evidence: Driven: stored 'notes' as 2.7M characters of invalid JSON and reloaded. The backup write threw (quota, because the copy doubles usage), 'notes-backup' was null, yet the status read 'The unreadable data was kept under "notes-backup"'. Clicking New note then replaced 'notes' (2,700,001 chars) with a 122-char object. The comment's claim that the load message says so is false: loadNotes lines 48, 53 and 67 state success unconditionally.
failing_case: A user whose notes blob is corrupt and larger than half the storage quota reloads the page. The page claims the data was kept in 'notes-backup'. Nothing was kept. The first New note or edit overwrites the corrupt original, and all of it is permanently lost.
remediation: Make backupRaw return whether it succeeded. If it failed, do not overwrite STORAGE_KEY (hold the app read-only or refuse saves) and tell the user the data could not be backed up and how to export it. Claim 'kept' only on success.

title: A note created while a search is active is selected but not shown in the list
evidence: Driven: typed 'zzz' in search, clicked New note; the list had 0 rows while the editor showed 'Untitled' selected.
failing_case: With any non-empty search that does not match 'Untitled', New note opens an editor for a note that appears nowhere in the list, and the only way to see it is to clear the search.
remediation: Clear the search box and re-render in createNote before selecting the new note.
